distribution.narrative: Smith et al. (2020) records Hainan, Xizang, Yunnan and Taiwan. Beaver & Liu (2010) independently reports the first Taiwan record in its treatment, including Ilan and Nantou localities; the current promoted distribution therefore remains unchanged.

host_note: No specific host taxon is promoted. Beaver & Liu (2010) states that the species uses seven genera in six families, but the genera are not enumerated in the curated source field; this broad host-use statement is retained as context only.
taxonomy_summary: The current accepted identity is Diuncus corpulentus (Eggers, 1930).

taxonomic_history.name: Diuncus corpulentus
taxonomic_history.note: Current accepted name in the integrated taxonomic backbone.

nomenclature_note: Canonical identity follows integrated taxonomic backbone: Diuncus corpulentus (Eggers, 1930), VSN_2389. Beaver & Liu (2010) provides additional Taiwan evidence without changing the accepted identity.
